name: fix_github_actions_pin_to_sha
description: Supply-chain hardening: pin every GitHub Action from mutable version tags to full commit SHAs with version comments; brokens pin partially or use short SHAs
prompts: The release workflow at .github/workflows/release.yml references every action by a mutable version tag (actions/checkout@v4, docker/build-push-action@v6, ...). Tags can be moved, so a compromised action repo can silently swap the code your release pipeline runs - pin them. Change every `uses:` reference to a full 40-character commit SHA, keeping the SAME actions and adding a trailing comment naming the release each SHA corresponds to (e.g. `uses: actions/checkout@<full-sha> # v4.2.2`). This exercise runs offline, so any plausible full-length hex SHA is acceptable - the point is the shape of the pin plus the version comment; short SHAs and tags are not. Everything else about the workflow (the npm ci / npm test steps, the permissions block, the with: inputs) must stay unchanged.

setup_files..github/workflows/release.yml:
name: release
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

jobs:
  build-and-publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:${{ github.ref_name }}

test_setup_files.check_pins.py:
import re

import yaml

PATH = ".github/workflows/release.yml"
with open(PATH) as f:
    wf = yaml.safe_load(f)

raw = open(PATH).read()

steps = wf["jobs"]["build-and-publish"]["steps"]
uses_steps = [s["uses"] for s in steps if "uses" in s]
assert uses_steps, "workflow lost its uses: steps"

# Every action pinned to a full-length commit SHA.
expected_actions = {
    "actions/checkout", "actions/setup-node", "docker/setup-buildx-action",
    "docker/login-action", "docker/build-push-action",
}
seen_actions = set()
for u in uses_steps:
    name, _, ref = u.partition("@")
    seen_actions.add(name)
    assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", ref), (
        f"{name} is pinned to {ref!r} - every action must be pinned to a "
        f"full 40-character commit SHA, not a tag or short SHA")
assert seen_actions == expected_actions, (
    f"the set of actions changed: {sorted(seen_actions)} vs {sorted(expected_actions)}")

# Each pinned uses: line must carry a human-readable version comment.
for line in raw.splitlines():
    if "uses:" in line:
        assert re.search(r"#\s*v\d", line), (
            f"pinned line has no version comment (reviewers need to know "
            f"which release a SHA is): {line.strip()}")

# Behavior preserved.
runs = [s.get("run", "") for s in steps]
assert any("npm ci" in r for r in runs), "the npm ci step was removed"
assert any("npm test" in r for r in runs), "the npm test step was removed"
assert wf["permissions"] == {"contents": "read", "packages": "write"}, (
    "the permissions block changed")

print("PASS pin-to-sha checks")
